author: reek
body: The same message, transcript form. Twelve bytes of header on the wire; four in the hash.

author: reek
body: And the assertion that matters: these are NOT the same bytes. If this ever reads same=True, someone has "simplified" the transcript to reuse the wire encoding and the handshake will never interoperate again.

author: reek
body: A truncated header is not a message. A datagram protocol is handed rubbish constantly, and reading past the end of it is the attack.

author: reek
body: A header whose fragment_length runs past the datagram is a lie. Trusting it is an out-of-bounds read.

author: reek
body: A parsed message must hash to the same transcript bytes the sender put in. This is the round trip that matters: not wire-to-wire, but wire-to-TRANSCRIPT.

author: reek
body: A Finished that verifies proves the peer holds the same handshake secret. It does NOT prove who the peer is -- there is still no peer authentication anywhere in this stack. A wrong transcript must fail.
